patch_resolves_note: The fixed nDPI source adds `if(packet->payload_packet_len > 4)` before either four-byte Amazon signature check. On the original one-byte witness, the fixed original still reaches `tcp_signature_guard` with `packet->payload_packet_len == 1` but never reaches `tcp_signature_second_byte`; the closest boundary mutation with a five-byte `FE ED FA CE 00` payload reaches the protected second-byte event genuinely on both builds while satisfying the required predicate.

root_cause_criterion.description: Before the TCP `FE ED FA CE` signature comparison can evaluate its second byte, the payload-length predicate `packet->payload_packet_len > 4` must already hold at `ndpi_check_amazon_video()`.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable original reaches `tcp_signature_guard` with `packet->payload_packet_len == 1` and still reaches `tcp_signature_second_byte`, so the required predicate is violated. The fixed original guards the original case, and the five-byte boundary witness reaches `tcp_signature_second_byte` genuinely with `packet->payload_packet_len == 5`.

nodes.description: At the second TCP signature-byte comparison, the accessed index `1` is already outside the available payload span because `packet->payload_packet_len <= 1`.
The first Amazon TCP signature-byte comparison succeeds because `packet->payload[0]` equals the in-source constant `0xFE`.

edges.description: The same short `packet->payload_packet_len` observed at the missing guard is still the length in force when the second-byte comparison is reached.
The same first signature byte that matches `0xFE` at line 38 remains the byte in force when control advances to the line-39 second-byte comparison.
The parser-derived payload length computed from the TCP header reaches the Amazon signature guard unchanged.
edges.evidence: In the vulnerable original case, `payload_len_computed.payload_packet_len == tcp_signature_guard.payload_packet_len` (1 == 1).
